findings.summary: The page relies on validators, ETag and 304 revalidation before the validator pages (5-7) define them.
findings.evidence: "no-cache: HTML shells, checked but a cheap 304"; code block "ETag: \"v7\"" / "# next use sends If-None-Match" with note "no-cache still needs a validator"
findings.fix: Add a one-line forward definition on this page: a validator (ETag or Last-Modified) lets the cache ask the origin whether its copy changed, and a 304 means "unchanged, reuse your copy". Link it to pages 5-7.

findings.summary: The page teaches testing 304s with If-None-Match curl commands and symptom diagnosis two pages before conditional requests are explained.
findings.evidence: "Send `curl -H 'If-None-Match: \"v7\"' -I` and expect a 304"; checklist "Send it back as `If-None-Match`"; table "Always 200, never 304 | server ignores validator"
findings.fix: Move the validation checklist, curl test and symptom table to after "Conditional Requests and 304" (page 7 or 8). Keep only choosing the validator type on page 6.

findings.summary: Heuristic freshness depends on Last-Modified, which is undefined at this point, and it sits under the unrelated heading "What gets stored".
findings.evidence: Code block shows "Last-Modified: Sun, 06 Sep 2026"; under heading "4. What gets stored": "No lifetime set? ==Heuristic freshness== guesses ~10% of (Date − Last-Modified)"
findings.fix: Move the stale and heuristic bullets into the section "3. Hit, miss, fresh, stale". Say that Last-Modified is a header giving when the resource last changed (covered on page 5).

findings.summary: The request-side no-cache directive is used here but not defined until the next page.
findings.evidence: Table row "Request `no-cache` | demand fresh copy | hard reload"
findings.fix: Add a short note "no-cache is explained on the next page", or move this row to page 3.

findings.summary: Heading "4. Common mistakes" already appears on page 2.
findings.fix: Fine if the two pages cover different topics; rename if they do not.

findings.summary: The bfcache callout contradicts itself and overstates how the cache behaves.
findings.evidence: "Back/forward cache can restore a page whatever the headers say, unless no-store is set."
findings.fix: Reword to: "The back/forward cache can restore a page even if it is no-cache. Cache-Control: no-store usually makes a page ineligible, but browsers differ and are changing this, so test it."

findings.summary: The note says no-cache needs a validator. It doesn't; without one the cache just refetches in full.
findings.fix: Change to: "no-cache without a validator forces a full refetch; add an ETag or Last-Modified to get cheap 304s."

findings.summary: The table uses the immutable directive and a one-year max-age before page 4 introduces them.
findings.fix: Remove the row from this page, or mark it "see next page".

findings.summary: The page explains why immutable matters in terms of conditional requests, which are not introduced until page 7.
findings.evidence: "Browser skips revalidation, even on reload"; "Normal reload sends a conditional request per asset"
findings.fix: Reword as "a normal reload re-checks every asset with the origin", or defer the detail until after page 7.

findings.summary: The text says caches use both validators, but when a request carries both, If-None-Match takes precedence and If-Modified-Since is ignored. The Last-Modified example date is also in the future relative to the page's own Date header, which the page says breaks caching.
findings.evidence: "If both sent, caches use both"; "Last-Modified: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 07:28:00 GMT" (the page's Date is 06 Oct 2026)
findings.fix: Say "Send both; when a request has both, If-None-Match is evaluated and If-Modified-Since is ignored." Use a past Last-Modified date in the example.

findings.summary: If-None-Match, 304 and If-Range are used as known terms before the conditional-request pages define them.
findings.evidence: Flow diagram "Sends validator / If-None-Match" and "304 or 200"; "ETag wins for If-None-Match matching"; "`If-Range` and Range need strong validators; weak fails"
findings.fix: Add a one-line forward reference: "the cache sends the validator back in If-None-Match (ETag) or If-Modified-Since (Last-Modified); details on page 7". Defer the If-Range gotcha until page 7, where it is defined.

findings.summary: The per-variant ETag example uses Vary: Accept-Encoding before the Vary page explains it.
findings.fix: Add a note that Vary tells caches to store separate copies per request header value and is covered on page 9, or drop the Vary line here.

findings.summary: Vary: * is not limited to shared caches; no cache may reuse a stored response without going back to the origin.
findings.evidence: "`Vary: *` means shared caches must always revalidate"
findings.fix: Write: "`Vary: *` means a stored response can never be matched to a later request, so every cache must go to the origin; avoid it."
